tasks.locator: Introduction › Controversies in drug safety testing, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs
tasks.extracted: Relayed, without data of the author's own: critics' concerns that testing at best gives an artificial impression of safety (citing Winstock et al., 2001), that results may be inadequate, that dealers may use services for quality control, that services focus on contaminants rather than risky behaviours, and that testing may reduce the deterrent value and raise the appeal of drugs by making them seem safer; and, on the other side, that two decades of Dutch testing and alerts had no perverse effect on drug use or drug-related deaths, and that there is no evidence that drug prevalence, initiation or mortality rose in European countries with drug safety testing compared with those without (citing Benschop et al., 2002; Brunt, 2012; Hungerbuehler et al., 2011). These are country-level comparisons of services, not of kits.
